messages:
From: Samir Khatri <samir@stratohealth.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-05-09T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sizing inputs for Dedicated proposal?

Hi Rishi —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. The engineering team asked me to pull together the basic traffic/usage information so you can put together a Dedicated sizing proposal. Quick high-level answers below and I attached a small telemetry sample from last week.

- Primary product: patient Q&A chat + summarization on clinician dashboard (mix of short prompts + long responses)
- Typical daily active users (DAU): ~18k; estimated peak concurrency: ~1.2k sessions (our current spike observed ~16:00 PT)
- Prompt/response: prompts are short (median ~50–80 tokens); responses average ~350–500 tokens depending on query complexity
- Session duration: sessions are single-request for ~70% of traffic; 30% are multi-turn (avg 3 turns)
- Streaming: yes for longer summaries (we'd like token streaming)
- Persistence: we keep transcripts for 90 days; KV cache not persisted beyond session
- SLA targets: p95 generation latency <300ms, p99 <700ms (soft), but we'd accept initial trial at 1s p99 while we optimize prompts

Attached: telemetry_sample_202504.csv (scrubbed). Happy to answer a more detailed questionnaire if you have one — engineering can export more telemetry.

Best,
Samir
Lead Platform Engineer
StratoHealth

Subject: Dedicated sizing questionnaire + template

Hi Samir —

Thanks for the telemetry sample — that helps. I put together a compact questionnaire and attached an XLSX template that our capacity-sizing engine ingests. If you can fill columns A–G it will cut our scoping time in half. Quick asks below; the template has examples.

1) Traffic shape
- Peak concurrent sessions (observed and how long the peak lasts)
- Average requests/sec at peak
- Burst profile: percentage of traffic in 1-min, 5-min, 15-min windows

2) Prompt & response metrics
- Median prompt tokens; 90th percentile prompt tokens
- Median response tokens; 90th percentile response tokens
- Fraction of requests requiring streaming (yes/no + percent)

3) Session & cache behavior
- Fraction of multi-turn sessions and average turns
- KV cache reuse rate across turns (approx %)
- Any long-running sessions ( > 60s generation window )

4) SLA and fallbacks
- Target p95/p99 latency targets for interactive flows
- Acceptable fallback model (smaller variant) if primary unavailable

5) Data & compliance
- Data residency needs, retention windows, and any KMS/HSM constraints

6) Perf validation
- Do you have a synthetic harness we can run against a staging endpoint? If yes, provide endpoints and a test key TTL.

Attachment: dedicated-sizer-template.xlsx

When you return the sheet, we will run a short occupancy analysis and come back with an initial fleet footprint (GPU-sku mix, expected p99 under target batching, and an early cost estimate). I'll also include a proposed 4-step MOP as Rishi suggested.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Staff Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: dedicated-sizer-template.xlsx]

Thanks Marissa — attached you will find the template filled with the fields you requested (I exported the week of 2025-05-02 to 2025-05-08). Answers inline below the questions on the sheet. Highlights:

- Peak concurrent sessions: 1,200 sustained for ~12 minutes (observed between 15:48–16:00 PT daily).
- Requests/sec at peak: ~220 RPS sustained during that 12-minute window.
- Burst profile: 1-min = 48% of peak; 5-min = 82% of peak; 15-min = 95% of peak.

- Median prompt tokens: 60; 90th percentile prompt tokens: 120.
- Median response tokens: 380; 90th percentile response tokens: 720.
- Streaming: ~22% of requests (long summaries).

- Multi-turn sessions: 30% of sessions; avg 3.1 turns.
- KV cache reuse: ~68% reuse across turns for the 30% multi-turn subset.
- Long-running generations: rare (<1%); max observed generation windows ~4s.

- SLA targets: p95 < 300ms; p99 soft target 700ms (we can accept 1s during trial). Fallback: smaller LLM variant acceptable for degraded mode.

- Data residency: US only; retention 90 days. KMS: AWS KMS required for keys in staging/production.

- Perf harness: yes — we can provide a staged endpoint with a test key good for 72 hours. Adding that to the attachment (staging_harness_info.txt).

Attached: filled_dedicated-sizer-template.xlsx, staging_harness_info.txt, sample_telemetry_202504.csv

Let us know if you need anything else.

Samir — thanks for the fast turnaround and the filled template. Quick summary and proposed MOP below; please confirm dates and we'll lock in a perf window.

Summary (what we heard)
- Peak concurrency: 1,200 sessions sustained ~12 minutes/day (220 RPS)
- Token mix: prompt median 60 / response median 380; ~22% streaming; 30% multi-turn with 68% KV reuse
- Retention / compliance: US-only, 90-day retention, AWS KMS
- SLA target: p95 <300ms; p99 soft 700ms (trial acceptance 1s p99)

Proposed initial footprint (trial) — high-level
- Staging perf run: small cluster (6x H100-equivalent) to validate model variant and batching heuristics against your harness
- Pilot reserved capacity: target commit equivalent to 18–22 H100-equivalent GPUs (we will provide SKU mix options) — rationale: occupancy analysis suggests this will meet targeted p95 with observed token mix and 22% streaming assuming batching and KV cache reuse
- Costing & cadence: 30-day trial with perf validation -> 90-day pilot pricing with optional scale-up at month 2 if traffic increases

Mutual Action Plan (4 steps)
1) Data handoff (this week): Samir to share filled template + staging harness endpoint + test key (72h TTL) — DONE
2) Perf run (week 1): Redwood SE runs perf harness on staging cluster (we will provision internal perf nodes) — propose Tue 2025-05-13 10:00 PT. Please confirm or propose alternate window.
3) Validate & tune (week 2): Review perf results, iterate on prompt length/streaming knobs, quantization/kvcache settings. SE deliverables: expected p95/p99 and recommended SKU mix.
4) Commitment & contract (week 3): Lock pilot reserved capacity, commercial terms, data residency/KMS annex, and schedule production cutover.

Next steps for this thread:
- Samir: confirm perf window and provide test key + any throttles we should honor during perf run.
- Marissa / Priyom: I'll need an occupancy back-of-envelope in the thread by EOD today so I can draft the term sheet.

Thanks all — excited to get this into a perf run.

—Rishi
